title: Searching perturbation dictionaries with RNA fingerprints - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A research highlight on RNA fingerprinting (Grabski and colleagues, Cell), a statistical framework that matches new single-cell transcriptional responses to reference perturbation dictionaries, helping interpret large single-cell datasets.

insights.claim: Single-cell perturbation dictionaries, which catalogue transcriptional responses to biological and chemical stimuli, are becoming a tool for mechanistic interpretation of large single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, but matching a cell state to a known perturbation remains hard.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Interpretation, not data generation, is the bottleneck in single-cell drug discovery; analysis tools that close this gap have value.

insights.claim: Grabski and colleagues, writing in Cell, describe RNA fingerprinting, a statistical framework that learns denoised perturbation signatures from a reference dictionary and matches query cells to them using a Bayesian approach inspired by genome-wide association methods.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Borrowing statistical genetics methods for single-cell analysis is a reusable pattern for computational biology platforms.
insights.locator: RNA fingerprinting uses a two-stage statistical approach

insights.claim: On ground-truth datasets, RNA fingerprinting accurately matched known perturbations within and across cell types, scaled to genome-wide datasets and inferred combinatorial perturbations.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Cross-cell-type and combinatorial inference supports using perturbation atlases for mechanism-of-action and target deconvolution in drug screens.
insights.locator: Using ground-truth datasets, the authors show
